narrative_passages.title: Owners of the garden
narrative_passages.treatment_reason: Read after the harvest (68:17-27); the play does the opposite of the owners: the gate is opened for those in need first. The owners and the ruin of the garden are never shown.

summary_for_children: Al-Qalam means The Pen. It praises the Prophet's (peace be upon him) great character and tells of garden owners who planned to keep everything from the poor and lost their garden.
world_title: The Pen and the Burnt Garden
environment_concept: A pen and inkwell (68:1), a garden ready to harvest at dawn (68:17) and a garden that looks reaped (68:20).
architecture_and_scenery: A desk with pen and ink, a garden at dawn, a ruined garden.

activities.name: Share the harvest
activities.description: Carry four baskets from the garden to share.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

depiction_rules: No prophet, person or representation of Allah is shown. Unseen realities are never pictured. Interactive activities are labelled as adaptations.

unique_world.visual_theme: A walled orchard of fig trees with a stone gate and a bell, on harvest morning

primary_mechanic.text: Open the gate and ring the bell before harvesting (picking first is refused, recalling the owners of 68:24); then pick each tree from its branches and leave the fallen fruit for gleaners (picking it up is refused).

unique_world.narrative_structure: A reading on the lane, the gate and the harvest, then a reading among the trees
world_assets: fruit on branches and fallen fruit
environment_behaviour: fruit leaves the branches as each tree is picked; fallen fruit stays
unique_world.learning_objective: Know the story of the garden owners who would not share (68:17-27)

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Owners of the Garden
story_library.children_narration: A group of garden owners planned to harvest their fruits early so that the poor would receive nothing. But when they reached their garden, they discovered that it had been destroyed. They recognized that their plan had been wrong. Their story teaches us to remember Allah and avoid selfishness.

world_idea.title: The Orchard of Generosity
world_idea.description: Explore a beautiful orchard and its changed condition. Help create a fair sharing plan through an educational activity inspired by the parable.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
